description: Replaces a run's games_enriched rows transactionally, so re-running enrichment after a parameter change is idempotent (ADR-009).
signature: def write_enriched(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, frame: pd.DataFrame) -> int
docstring:
Replace the enriched-feature rows for a run.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    run_id: The run these rows belong to.
    frame: A DataFrame whose columns match games_enriched's non-key columns exactly (appid plus every derived/raw feature column listed in 01_storage.module_spec.json). NULL/NaN values are written as SQL NULL, never coerced to 0 or an empty string.

Returns:
    The number of rows written (len(frame)).

Raises:
    StorageError: If frame is missing a required column, or run_id does not exist.
preconditions: frame contains an 'appid' column with no duplicate values
every non-nullable column in the games_enriched schema is present in frame (even if all-NULL for that run)
postconditions: All prior games_enriched rows for run_id are gone and replaced atomically by frame's rows within a single transaction (DELETE then INSERT, or equivalent, never leaving a mixed old/new state visible to a concurrent reader under WAL)
NaN values in frame become SQL NULL, never 0 or ''
Calling write_enriched twice in a row with the same frame produces byte-for-byte identical stored rows (idempotence, per the enrichment module's own invariant)

edge_cases.expected_behavior: writes zero rows and returns 0 without raising, per the module spec's own edge case

edge_cases.input: frame missing a required column, e.g. no 'complexity_score' column at all

edge_cases.expected_behavior: StorageError, since (run_id, appid) is the primary key

edge_cases.input: A NaN value in a float column (e.g. complexity_score for a row with too much missing data)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: stored as SQL NULL, read back as None via read_enriched, never as 0.0

unit_tests.name: test_write_then_read_preserves_dtypes_and_nulls
unit_tests.description: A frame with a NaN complexity_score round-trips through write_enriched/read_enriched with None preserved.
unit_tests.expected: read_enriched shows complexity_score is None for that row

unit_tests.name: test_empty_frame_writes_zero_rows
unit_tests.description: An empty DataFrame with correct columns writes 0 rows.

inputs.frame: empty DataFrame with full column set

unit_tests.name: test_rerun_replaces_prior_rows
unit_tests.description: Writing a new frame for a run_id that already has rows removes the old ones entirely.
unit_tests.expected: read_enriched returns exactly the second frame's rows, none from the first
